result.title: Reliability-Aware Probabilistic Fusion for Multimodal Learning with Incomplete Evidence
result.summary: Multimodal inputs may be missing or degraded, raising distinct questions of evidence availability and trust. We introduce a reliability-aware Gaussian Product-of-Experts (PoE) in which an input-dependent reliability weight tempers each modality's latent precision, while missing experts are omitted. We characterize how reliability and availability affect posterior information and expert influence. Across two clinical multimodal tasks, the full framework remains competitive with complete inputs and achieves its clearest mean-AUROC advantage under modality absence, particularly on HAIM-MIMIC-MM. Ablations show a substantial gain from missing-aware training and an additional HAIM improvement from reliability weighting under matched PoE, missing-aware, and consistency training. Unseen test-time corruptions are used diagnostically and reveal modality-dependent reliability-weight and latent-uncertainty responses, including failure under severe degradation. Thus, reliability weighting provides an explicit evidence-control mechanism, while learning dependable quality signals remains an open challenge.

AI.brief_summary: 提出可靠性感知的高斯专家乘积融合，用输入相关的可靠性权重调节各模态 latent precision，并直接省略缺失专家；在两个临床多模态任务上验证其完整输入与模态缺失场景的表现，并用测试时损坏分析可靠性响应。
AI.relevance_reason: 其按证据可用性与可信度调节潜在精度、并显式去除缺失证据的机制，可供核查如何用于 LVR 的视觉证据筛选与退化时的 LOOK/STOP 决策；但论文不涉及 latent 推理状态的生成或训练。
